result.title: Needwise: Generation-Free Conversational Recommendation from Need-Level Typed Decisions
result.summary: Conversational recommenders must rank items against needs that catalogs record only in part, while users add, withdraw and reverse needs and switch between requests. LLM rankers re-read the dialogue at every turn: they are slow, and their ordering does not show which needs an item meets. We show that a conversational recommender can be built from typed decisions instead: named questions over fixed options, answered with option probabilities rather than generated text. On each turn, one typed request maps the message onto the catalog's fields, keeps what no field expresses in the user's words, and decides how the turn changes each earlier need. Needwise then ranks candidates must-first: the needs on the kind of item, its place and its price form a tier, and within it one holistic decision and need-level verdicts (supported, contradicted or unknown) are combined with equal weight (Needwise-HF). With the graded attributes withheld from the records, so that needs must be inferred from names, descriptions and reviews, Needwise-HF ranks Google Local requests significantly better than GPT-6 Sol (0.383 against 0.343 nDCG@10) and is not significantly different from the strongest LLM ranker on Google Local and Yelp; these comparisons keep their sign under every treatment of unrecorded attributes we test. It costs a fraction of GPT-6 Sol's API price and answers in 2.5 s at the median on Google Local, against 5.6 s for GPT-6 Sol. In conversations, the typed state keeps the ranking across switches and returns, but it recognizes only 19-27% of withdrawn needs.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Needwise，用固定选项上的具名问题（typed decisions）替代生成式 LLM 重读对话：每轮把消息映射到目录字段、保留无法字段化的用户原话，并更新既有需求状态，再按「必须项优先」的分层与需求级判定（支持／矛盾／未知）排序候选。
AI.relevance_reason: 其类型化需求状态的跨轮维护与「支持／矛盾／未知」级判定，可能为 LVR 中结构化推理状态表示与视觉证据筛选的表述提供概念参照；但该工作不涉及视觉或 latent 推理，迁移价值需核查。
